howto.goal: Join your top side to your bottom side with an unbroken chain of your stones before the other side joins left to right.
howto.setup: An 11 by 11 rhombus. Light joins top to bottom, dark joins left to right. Light moves first.

sections.title: No draws
sections.text: Every full board has exactly one connected side, so a Hex game always ends with a winner.

sections.title: Chains
sections.text: Stones touch along their six edges. A chain that reaches both of your sides wins.

sections.title: Blocking
sections.text: You cannot take a stone back, so a move both extends your chain and blocks theirs is strong.

controls: Click any empty cell to place your stone.
The ringed cell is where this lesson wants you.
Undo in a learning game takes back your last move and the computer's reply.

frames.say: A chain reaching the far side wins.

demo.intro: Watch the computer play itself. Light is building top to bottom; dark builds left to right.

lines.say: Empty board. Light wants the middle, because the middle is shortest to both sides.
Light takes f6, the centre cell.
Dark answers beside it at g6, starting its own line across the board.
Light extends at e6 — a chain of two.
Dark pushes at f7, blocking the light chain's path down the board.
Light steps around at e7, keeping the chain connected.
Dark blocks at g5. Notice both sides now threaten a route.

demo.outro: The side that keeps one connected line wins. In Play & Learn you make the same first moves yourself.

steps.say: You are Light and move first. Click the middle of the board to place your first stone.
Place your next stone so it touches one of your stones along an edge. If the swap took your first stone, start a fresh chain.
Build a line that reaches both of your sides. Top to bottom is yours.
If the computer blocks you, go around it — never leave a gap in your chain.
